title: Token Surge Scarcity Meter & Pricing Patterns for Console Cost Views
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a console-level token-cost panel that combines a live "scarcity meter" for token surge events with token-level cost breakdown, attribution, and export flows. The feature is intended for platform engineers and SREs to detect short-term token demand spikes, understand per-route and per-model unit economics, and export attribution slices for chargeback and pricing simulation. Deliverables: interactive Figma prototype, acceptance criteria, export spec (CSV/NDJSON), engineering integration notes, and two pricing pattern mockups (rate-bands and surge-slab).
acceptance_criteria: Scarcity meter shows current token consumption vs reserved capacity and projected 15m & 1h burn-rate with clear color states (normal | warming | scarce | critical)
Cost breakdown table surfaces per-token unit cost by model.variant and by route with sortable columns (tokens, unit_cost_usd, total_cost_usd, invocations)
Attribution view allows filtering by time window, route, model, and "prompt template" tag and supports grouping by customer project or org label
Export flow supports CSV and NDJSON with sample schema and toggles for include_prompt_text (opt-in) and anonymize_user_ids
Prototype includes two pricing UI patterns: continuous rate-band slider and discrete surge-slab editor, with documentation of application semantics and upgrade/downgrade UX
Design includes error/fallback states for missing data and guidance text for sampling tradeoffs when full per-invocation logging is disabled
prototypes: Compact mode: single-line scarcity meter + sparkline + top-3 cost contributors
Expanded mode: time-range selector, stacked area tokens by model, per-route cost table, verbatim attribution panel
Export wizard: step 1 choose window/filters, step 2 select columns & anonymization, step 3 delivery (download or push to S3)
engineering_notes: Required backend fields per invocation: timestamp, account_id, route_id, model_id, model_variant, token_count_input, token_count_output, cost_cents, latency_ms, prompt_template_tag
Support sampled logs: when sampling is enabled, UI shows an estimated confidence interval for totals and per-cell extrapolation factor
Data latency constraint: scarcity meter must tolerate up to 30s ingestion delay; show last_ingest_timestamp and staleness indicator
Performance: table pagination for >50k rows, server-side sorting and aggregation endpoints required
Export: NDJSON should include one record per invocation; CSV should include aggregated row mode (per-route or per-model)
decisions: Use combined visualization: stacked tokens time-series overlaid with reserved capacity band to make scarcity intuitive
Pricing pattern preference: expose both rate-band slider for day-to-day tweaks and surge-slab editor for predictable overage tiers
Default export anonymization: omit prompt text by default; user must opt-in and acknowledge data retention guidance
Show per-token unit cost to three decimal places (USD) to make microcost visible without noisy precision
tradeoffs: Sampling vs accuracy: sampling reduces cost and ingestion pressure but requires UI complexity to explain extrapolation; chosen to default to full logging when account is enterprise and sampling otherwise
Many columns vs simplicity: initial MVP exposes a curated set of columns (route, model, tokens, unit_cost, total_cost, invocations) with advanced export allowing full schema
Real-time UI refresh vs backend load: scarcity meter refresh interval defaults to 15s but configurable per org to avoid overload
